rows.name: Deep Voodoo
rows.basis: Variety, 2022-12-20: "The funding was led by Connect Ventures, an investment partnership between CAA and venture-capital firm New Enterprise Associates (NEA)", Deep Voodoo's first outside capital ($20M); AWN, 2022-12-21, same. Connect Ventures I, L.P. is on NEA's Form ADV Schedule 7.B (coordinator's correction), so this is NEA fund money (T1). Changed from reject.

rows.name: Grovo
rows.basis: Wikipedia: "In May 2011, Grovo secured seed funding from Krishna 'Kittu' Kolluri, general partner at New Enterprise Associates" with other individuals; a partner's personal check, no NEA fund named.

rows.name: Music AI (Moises)
rows.basis: Music Business Worldwide, 2025-01-22: the $40M Series A "was led by Connect Ventures – an investment partnership between ... CAA and venture capital firm New Enterprise Associates (NEA) – along with Brazilian investor monashees"; Connect's own site lists Moises. Changed from reject.

rows.name: Jomboy Media
rows.basis: Dodger Blue, 2022-05-06: the $5M round came through Connect Ventures, "Creative Artists Agency (CAA) and global venture capital firm New Enterprise Associates (NEA)", with Connect's Adam Friedman joining the board; THR (2026-01-26) lists Jomboy Media among Connect's investments. Changed from reject.

rows.name: TMRW Sports
rows.basis: SportsPro, 2024-06: "Dynasty Equity and Connect Ventures co-lead" the Series A, and Connect "also co-led the initial fundraising round for TMRW" (THR, 2022-11-02: "TMRW Sports Scores Investments From CAA's Connect Ventures"); on Connect's own portfolio page. Changed from reject.

rows.name: Compiere
rows.basis: Compiere press release, 2006-06-20: "Compiere, Inc. ... announced that it has secured $6 million in funding from New Enterprise Associates (NEA)", its first outside round, with NEA partners Vladimir Jacimovic and Harry Weller joining the board (Wikipedia's source for the same sentence).

rows.name: Vuze
rows.basis: TechCrunch, 2007-12-18: Vuze, "previously known as Azureus, has raised $20M in a Series C round of funding led by New Enterprise Associates (NEA)" (Wikipedia cites the Business Wire release of 2007-12-19 for the same round).

rows.name: Uptake
rows.basis: Business Insider via Yahoo Finance, 2017-02-01: "Uptake Technologies' other investments include Lefkofsky's own investment firm Lightbank, New Enterprise Associates, and ... Caterpillar"; Wikipedia: the $45M round of 2015-10-27 was "led by GreatPoint Ventures and existing investors including New Enterprise Associates" (NYT, 2015-10-27, not fetchable). Not on NEA's site in any era.

rows.name: Niroda Therapeutics
rows.basis: The firm's own CMS draft (dated 2026-07-22, unpublished, nea.com/portfolio/niroda still 404 on 2026-09-30) lists "Niroda Therapeutics ... developing non-opioid pain treatments", stage Early, status Private, investment type Current, NEA team Scott Gottlieb, Ali Behbahani, J.C. Lopez. No round is announced: the Korea Herald (2025-12-18) names founders Population Health Partners, F-Prime and Lilly Asia Ventures, and BB Biotech's Q2 2026 slides add Niroda as a new private position, so a 2026 private round exists; an unannounced deal carried by a draft, flagged for the judge.

rows.name: Logic Modeling
rows.basis: The firm's own archived Synopsys page (captured 2013-12-12, first investment year 1994, Historic) reads "Software tools for electronic design automation. (Acquired Logic Modeling for stock 3/94)": NEA's Synopsys stock is the consideration for Logic Modeling (the synopsys row is already not_member under D8), so Logic Modeling is the member; the year NEA first invested in it is not on record (1994 is the sale).

rows.name: Everest Design Automation
rows.basis: Synopsys S-3 of 1998-11-25 registers shares its selling stockholders "acquired ... in connection with the acquisition by Synopsys ... of Everest Design Automation Inc.", listing "New Enterprise Associates VII, Limited Partnership" (163,400 shares), NEA Presidents Fund and NEA Ventures 1998; the same archived Synopsys page notes "Acquired Everest Design for stock 10/98". A second company behind the synopsys D8 row.

rows.name: Vela Pharmaceuticals
rows.basis: NEA's own Schedule 13D on Pharmos (2006): "NEA 10 acquired 1,880,824 shares of Common Stock ... on October 25, 2006 in exchange for 7,500,075 shares of Series D Convertible Preferred Stock ... of Vela Pharmaceuticals, Inc.": NEA 10 held Vela privately, so the base row pharmos (currently member on a 2013 site listing) is its sale consideration under D8. The year of NEA's Vela Series D purchase is not stated (2006 is the sale).

rows.name: Avivo Corporation
rows.basis: WebSideStory's registration rights agreement lists "NEW ENTERPRISE ASSOCIATES 10, L.P." and "NEA Ventures 2000, L.P." on Schedule B, the "AVIVO INVESTORS" granted rights in the agreement of May 4, 2005, the day WebSideStory completed its merger with "Avivo Corporation, a California corporation" (WebSideStory 8-K, 2005-05-05, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1091158/000095013705005390/a08744e8vk.htm). Correction to the brief: Avivo was bought by WebSideStory in 2005; Visual Sciences, LLC was a separate 2006 purchase. So websidestory-inc (member on NEA's 2005 13G) is Avivo's sale consideration under D8.

rows.name: Hydra Host

spv_decode.basis: BH = Bright Health. The SPV sold $129.3M and filed 2019-12-19; Bright Health's own Form D (in formd-issuer-rounds.json) has a $635M offering with first sale 2019-12-16, filed 2019-12-20. bright-health merges into neuehealth.

Same code, $67.3M. Bright Health announced its $500M Series E on 2020-09-22 "including significant investments by Tiger Global Management, T. Rowe Price Associates, Blackstone, NEA", quoting NEA's Mohamad Makhzoumi (PR Newswire).

SH = Strive Health. First sale 2023-04-25, $7.5M (a 2025-06-25 D/A raised it to $12.5M); Fierce Healthcare, 2023-05-31: "Strive Health clinches $166M from CVS Health Ventures and NEA" (headline; body 403).
Same code. Strive Health's $550M Series D (announced 2025-09-09): "The equity round was led by New Enterprise Associates (NEA)" (Pulse 2.0).

RP = Radiology Partners. First sale 2024-02-12, $244.57M; Radiology Partners raised $720M of growth equity in Feb 2024 (Radiology Business, 2024-02-22, headline) and Radiology Partners Holdings, LLC filed its own Form D 2024-03-07; the SPV's second Form D (2026-08-20) follows the issuer's Form D of 2026-07-15. WSJ, 2019: "NEA-Founded Radiology Startup Hits $4 Billion Valuation".

TS = Themis Solutions Inc., Clio's legal name ("Themis Solutions Inc. (dba Clio)", Blue Owl Capital Corp II 10-Q, 2026). First sale 2024-06-12, $155M (D/A 2024-08-02); Clio's "$900 million Series F investment round led by New Enterprise Associates (NEA)" was announced 2024-07-23 (William Blair).
Same code. The Logic, 2025-11-10: NEA "came in again to lead the latest round", Clio's US$500M Series G.

spv_decode.basis: First sale 2024-05-08, $65M from 20 investors. No NEA-announced round by a CH company near that date. Not CHAOS: NEA's first CHAOS money was the May 2025 Series C it led (citybiz, 2025-05-05). The BH/SH/RP pattern (initials of NEA healthcare growth positions) points to Curana Health (NEA's 2021 growth deal, raises unannounced) or Collective Health; both are base rows, so no candidate either way.

An Ontario, Canada limited partnership filed the same day as PLA 2025; its twin NEA 1M 2025 SPV names the same GP (NEA 1F 2025 SPV GP, LLC), so F and M read as feeder and master of one vehicle coded "1". No NEA round matched; an SPV is never a row and nothing points to a missing company.
